themes.summary: Crude fell on reports of renewed US-Iran contacts, but analysts (TD, GRM) say escalation risk keeps a floor and see no deal before the midterms.
Hormuz transits fell to 16, Iran threatens Sinokor vessels from Nov. 1, OMV lifted no UAE cargoes and the World Bank sees global oil production down more than 5% in 2026.

themes.theme: Strategic stock releases vs depleted inventories
themes.summary: Europe will release more than 42 million barrels, adding to the IEA program, while Shell, TotalEnergies and PetroChina cite low inventories needing restocking.
Dated Brent differential fell $6.20/b in four sessions to 6 cents/b, November North Sea and Midland cargoes went unsold, and Brent CFDs flipped to contango in the prompt.

themes.theme: High freight squeezing margins and runs
themes.summary: Shell, Repsol, Neste and Chinese refiners cite freight costs eroding margins; Sinopec and independents plan November run cuts.
YPF at a record 250,300 b/d, Vista and Repsol raising output, Petrobras record subsalt output, and US rigs up more than 50 since spring.
India says it faces no pressure to cut Russian crude after the Oct. 16 US waiver; Russian shipments to India were 1.64 million b/d in September versus a 2.43 million b/d June peak.
World Bank sees Brent $91/b in 2026 and $79/b in 2027, S&P Global Energy $95.43/b and $88.40/b, OMV above $95/b, and PetroChina expects Q4 prices to stay elevated.
